text:
siva: Heads up — seeing a weird spike in pending tiny-gpu pods in eu-west1c. Lots of pods stuck Pending on a handful of racks, others idle. Looks like inter-pod egress queueing is causing scheduler to avoid nodes and compact small pods onto same shelves, then preempt churn.

amanda: ugh. any recent scheduler rollout?

siva: not that I know of. kube-scheduler is stable. saw a firewall rule change earlier for an internal egress LB (PR #4821). could be coincidental.

siva: pasted the top pending pods and events:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n ai-serving -o wide | grep Pending | head
ai-job-rt-7b9c tiny  Pending 0/4  0  20m  eu-west1c-rack-12
ai-job-rt-8c6d tiny  Pending 0/4  0  18m  eu-west1c-rack-12
...
$ kubectl describe node eu-west1c-rack-12 | egrep -A3 "Taints|Allocatable"
Taints:  dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule
Allocatable: cpu=88 gpu=4 memory=384Gi
Events: PodPreempted -> 6 times in last 10m
```

chen: those repeated PodPreempted events are the clue — scheduler is trying to pack to reduce fragmentation but egress backpressure makes Kubelet evict and reschedule. result: tiny pods bounce and recompact.

jonah: can we quickly lift the preempt window and lower packing weight? i.e. temporarily increase preemptive-burst-limit and set binpacking score to favor spread for tiny pods.

amanda: how hard is that to change? need a chart?

chen: it's a configmap change for our scheduler-policy, then a rollout. low-risk but affects binpack heuristics across region.

maria: customer impact: we've had 3% tail latency increase for hosted API in eu-west1 and a small bump in GPU minutes because of re-deploy thrash. cost hit ~£600/day if it continues.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-3274 (eu-west1c pod scheduling surge). Severity: P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-3274

dina: can we do a targeted workaround first? maybe taint one stale rack as no-burst and drain tiny workloads there to stop the magnet.

jonah: good idea. tainting rack-12 as maintenance/no-burst will stop new tiny pods from landing and let autoscaler rebalance. i'll coordinate the drain window.

siva: +1. also suggest enabling prefix KV cache warmup for small-job model to reduce egress calls per start — reduces network pressure.

amanda: do we have a runbook step for reverting scheduler-policy?

chen: yes: 
1) update scheduler configmap with binpackSpread override for label "workload-size=tiny"
2) rollout kube-scheduler with 5m grace 
3) monitor pod pending and preempt events for 20m
4) rollback if we see negative impact on large-gang allocations

maria: prioritize avoiding large-gang fragmentation — any spread change must keep gang affinity for big models. we'll gate the change on existing integration test that simulates 8x GPU gangs.

jonah: I'll taint rack-12 now, run drain on non-critical tiny pods, and then prepare the config change for a canary rollout to eu-west1 only.

siva: tagging @oncall for visibility.

oncall-bot: @oncall-eng oncall notified: Siva triggered incident INC-2026-3274.

dina: after taint+drain, can we temporarily bump preemption budget so pods don't restart into the same rack? that should reduce immediate churn.

chen: yes, set preemptBudget=50 for tiny label for 30m. I'll push the patch to the scheduler-config repo and open PR.

amanda: keeping an eye on the dashboards. will report back in 15. :eyes:

siva: thanks all. quick checklist: taint rack-12 (jonah), bump preempt budget (chen), prepare scheduler-policy canary (jonah+chen), warm KV cache config (siva). follow-up meeting in 30m if things don't stabilize. :thumbsup:
